payload.headline: Two live security holes closed, three guards that proved nothing made falsifiable, one unstyled component found only by looking
payload.pattern: A guard must prove it can OBSERVE the violation, not merely pass. Three ATLAS guards were green while measuring nothing: a SOUL-invariant proof that compared a pure function against itself, an assertion checking for a string no renderer had ever emitted, and a propagation contract whose hand-typed regex matched the very text it was meant to reject. Proving the red once at commit time only proves that day. Build the falsifiability check INTO the test: a deliberately-violating control, asserted to move before the real subject is asserted not to, so it re-proves itself every run.
payload.secondPattern: A coverage set that does not derive from the thing it covers will be complete and wrong. The visual court reported a complete matrix while omitting the one route the session changed, because its page list is hand-maintained. Same shape as hand-registered root tests and a hand-maintained blocker taxonomy.

That template still declares the retired /500 v2 rubric, so every sync reverts any repo that has moved to CANON-009 SIL v3 (/1000, ten categories). Run it against the template and it will produce the corrected file; it is the fix, not just a description of one.

payload.headline: The census gating the data export was counting the wrong row, and the privacy roster already knew.
payload.lesson: A completeness claim scoped from the DECLARATIONS that seed a subject rather than from the subject. Three hand-typed rosters described one durable row, each internally consistent, none with a reader that knew the others existed.
transferable: Ask which direction your instruments error is CHEAP in, and tune toward that side: under-reporting is expensive when the consumer is a completeness claim.
A lexical scan must publish its MISS LIST and its REACH; a miss list alone is satisfiable by a scan that finds nothing.
A dead member on a safety roster is DECLARED, not deleted: removing a deny to settle an accounting staleness pays down bookkeeping with a safety guard.
Comments do not count as life: scan comment-stripped code, or the comments recording a defect keep its control green.

payload.headline: A gate guarding against an EXTERNAL actor must run server-side, not only in a local pre-push hook.
shipped: repo-contracts CI job enforcing the ownership boundary on push and pull_request
pnpm test:verified - direct children, inherited stdio, inner exit codes captured verbatim, verdict printed last so a truncating pipe reveals it
check-propagation-boundary-adoption.mjs - typed ADOPTED/REPORTED-NOT-ADOPTED/UNKNOWN verdict measured from the control plane
payload.finding: S329 declared an ownership boundary after template propagation clobbered five repo-owned files three times, then wired the guard into .husky/pre-push and nowhere else. ci.yml referenced it zero times. A contract written about an external actor could only fail for the one party that never triggers it.
payload.generalizable: When adding a guard, ask who it guards against and where that party commits arrive. If the answer is anyone other than you, it belongs in CI too.

payload.headline: A census scored 62 of 183 dispatch sites and printed unrecorded:0; a release gate read a self-report as verification
lessons: Any census must count its subject TWICE — once with the recogniser it scores by, once with a wider/dumber rule — and report the difference as UNSCORED. Without it, sites-I-can-read and sites-that-exist are the same number by construction, and a new dialect shrinks the denominator while every printed total stays green.

A verdict section must declare HOW it knows: positive (observed the intended path working), negative (observed the wrong path refused), or self-report (asked the subject about itself, which is not a control). An enforcement claim proven only by a refusal cannot tell a working gate from a shut door — both refuse.
A defect state measuring two facts with two owners is clearable by neither. Split by owner, and check the registry vocabulary before inventing one.

Widening a detector without widening its guard analysis converts a silence defect into an over-firing defect — strictly worse, because the silent one gets believed and the noisy one gets switched off.
